page: The Vultr vx1-m-192c-1536gb is a high-capacity virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is equipped with 192 dedicated AMD vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 1435.0 GB of system memory. This allocation provides approximately 7.47 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not feature any GPU accelerators and is provisioned with 1 GB of network-attached local storage, plus a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

With only 1 GB of network storage, this configuration is designed to interface with external storage systems rather than relying on local disks. This architecture prioritizes raw processing power and memory capacity, offering high resource density. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it provides a specialized environment for workloads that demand massive memory footprints and parallel processing capabilities without the added cost of large local solid-state drives.

This server is engineered for highly parallelized, memory-heavy operations. Suitable workloads include enterprise-grade databases, large-scale in-memory caching layers, big data analytics, and complex scientific simulations that require substantial memory and dedicated CPU cores.
